summary: This is a PHP API endpoint for managing blog article reactions (helpful/not helpful votes). It handles CORS validation, loads and saves vote counts from a JSON file, processes GET requests to retrieve vote data and POST requests to record new votes, and sends admin notifications with rate-limiting to prevent email spam.

explanations.2: This tells PHP to be strict about data types — if a function expects a string and gets something else, it will error instead of silently converting.
explanations.6: This checks if a .env file exists; if it does, parse it into an array of key-value pairs, otherwise use an empty array.
explanations.7: The `?:` operator means 'if parse_ini_file returns something falsy (like false or null), use an empty array instead'.
explanations.25: This checks if there's an Origin header (meaning it's a cross-origin request) AND that origin isn't in our whitelist — if so, reject it.
explanations.31: Only send CORS headers back if the request actually had an Origin header; same-origin requests don't have one.
explanations.38: Browsers send an OPTIONS request before certain cross-origin requests to ask if the server allows it; we respond with 204 (No Content) to say yes.
explanations.50: If the file doesn't exist or json_decode fails, return an empty array; the `?:` handles the falsy case.
explanations.55: Open the file in 'c+' mode, which creates it if it doesn't exist and opens it for reading and writing.
explanations.59: Lock the file exclusively so no other process can read or write to it while we're updating it.
explanations.60: Clear the file contents to 0 bytes so we can write fresh data without old content leftover.
explanations.70: Convert to lowercase, trim whitespace, then keep only lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and slashes.
explanations.74: The `never` return type means this function always exits and never returns normally — useful for type checking.
explanations.87: Check if enough time has passed since the last notification for this article; if not enough time has passed, skip the email.
explanations.94: Calculate the percentage of helpful votes; if there are no votes yet, default to 0 to avoid division by zero.
explanations.114: The `@` suppresses any error from mail() — if it fails, we just don't update the throttle file.
explanations.128: Check if the 'admin' query parameter exists in the URL (not just if it has a value).
explanations.137: Read raw POST body from php://input and decode it as JSON; if it fails, use an empty array.
explanations.153: If this article slug hasn't been voted on before, create its vote counter with both counts at zero.
